rationale: PINS `include("path")` AS `part_of`, AND PINS THE THREE SHAPES THAT ARE NOT. The contract (`src/ast/types.ts`, PartOf) is a file that shares the including unit's single scope and has no module identity — Julia's `include` is exactly that: it evaluates the file INSIDE the including module. The target is the BASENAME with its extension (`part.jl`), the spelling a file's own module symbol can carry, and the written path is kept in `meta.partPath`. THREE NEGATIVES, because a rule that fires on every call is not a measurement: (1) `include(dynamic)` names a VARIABLE, so no file is named — it stays a `calls` edge to `include` with `meta.isDynamicInclude`; (2) `include(joinpath("src", "joined.jl"))` is an EXPRESSION, not a string literal, so it also stays a call (and the inner `joinpath` call remains its own edge); (3) a module that DECLARES `include` shadows the builtin, and the planted `include = x -> x` turns the row back into a `calls` edge to the local binding with `meta.isShadowedInclude` — the conservative whole-file guard is shown firing rather than assumed unreachable. The forbid rows are the load-bearing half: no `part_of` may name `dynamic.jl`, `joined.jl` or `not-a-file.jl`, because no source text names those files as parts.

expectRelationships.comment: FIRE (1) — the plain literal path. `partRole` is mandatory on every row: this file carries the directive and names the part.
FIRE (2) — a path with a directory: the TARGET is the basename (a name a file symbol can carry), the written path is the evidence in `partPath`.
FIRE (3) — inside a callable. The include still belongs to the enclosing module's file set; the source is the callable that executes it.
NEGATIVE (1) read the right way — a variable path is a call to `include`, not a part edge.

NEGATIVE (2) — `joinpath(...)` is an expression, so the file is named by the program, not by the source. The OUTER `include` call on this line is the same (source, target) edge as line 7 and the lane's dedupe law keeps one row; the absence of a `part_of` is what the forbid row below pins.
NEGATIVE (3) — the module declares `include`, so the builtin is shadowed and the row is a call to the local binding.

forbidRelationships.comment: a variable path names no part
an expression path names no part
a shadowed include is a call, not a part
